title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Cross-boundary Greenhouse Gas Titles and Other Measures) Bill 2019
short_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Cross-boundary Greenhouse Gas Titles and Other Measures) Bill 2019

divisions.question: The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2020-02-11.102.1) to the usual [second reading motion](https://www.peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/), which is "*that the bill be read a second time*" (parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill). ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House notes the Government's failure to adequately promote the development and commercialisation of carbon reducing technologies".*

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the second reading of a bill to amend the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act, enabling single greenhouse gas titles for formations straddling state/territory and Commonwealth waters and granting NOPSEMA warrant-free inspection powers during oil pollution emergencies. The bill supports the Hydrogen Energy Supply Chain and CarbonNet projects, with the Australian government providing nearly $150 million in total funding.

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: The bill clarifies that regulatory levies apply to cross-boundary greenhouse gas titles, including parts in state or Northern Territory waters, and confirms the levies act applies to the Crown in right of each state and the Northern Territory, with retrospective effect to validate past levy payments by Victoria.

speeches.speaker: Joel Fitzgibbon
speeches.brief: The opposition supported the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment Bill 2019 but moved an amendment lamenting the government's failure to adequately promote carbon-reducing technologies, noting cuts to carbon capture and storage funding and a lack of economy-wide action on emissions reduction, electric vehicles, forestry abatement and hydrogen.

speeches.speaker: Katrina Allen
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Cross-Boundary Greenhouse Gas Titles and Other Measures) Bill 2019 simplifies cross-boundary greenhouse gas storage titles and strengthens the National Offshore Petroleum Safety Environmental Management Authority's response powers during oil spills. They highlighted the Morrison government's $500 million investment in hydrogen development, the National Hydrogen Strategy, and projects like CarbonNet and the Hydrogen Energy Supply Chain in Victoria's Latrobe Valley to support a carbon-neutral economy.

speeches.speaker: Matt Keogh
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment Bill 2019, arguing it creates a unified Commonwealth title for carbon capture and storage projects crossing state and Commonwealth waters, specifically aiding the Victorian CarbonNet and Hydrogen Energy Supply Chain projects in Bass Strait. They criticised the government for cutting $400 million from carbon-sequestration projects and lacking a comprehensive climate policy, while noting bipartisan Labor support for the bill as a small step forward.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Gee
speeches.brief: The Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Cross-boundary Greenhouse Gas Titles and Other Measures) Bill 2019 amends the OPGGS Act to enable single greenhouse gas titles straddling state and Commonwealth waters and to strengthen NOPSEMA’s oil spill emergency powers, including warrant-free inspections. The bill also supports the hydrogen export industry via the CarbonNet project, which has received nearly $150 million in government funding.
